title: The Empty Heart, or the Tao in its Operation
chinese: 自今及古，其名不去，以阅众甫。
pinyin: Kǒng dé zhī róng， wéi dào shì cóng。
Dào zhī wèi wù， wéi huǎng wéi hū。
Hū xī huǎng xī， qí zhōng yǒu xiàng；
Huǎng xī hū xī， qí zhōng yǒu wù。
Yǎo xī míng xī， qí zhōng yǒu jīng；
Qí jīng shèn zhēn， qí zhōng yǒu xìn。
Zì jīn jí gǔ， qí míng bù qù， yǐ yuè zhòng fǔ。
Wú hé yǐ zhī zhòng fǔ zhī zhuàng zāi？
english: The grandest forms of active force From Tao come, their only source. Tao Who can of Tao the nature tell? Tao Our sight it flies, our touch as well. Eluding sight, eluding touch, The forms of things all in it crouch; Eluding touch, eluding sight, There are their semblances, all right. Profound it is, dark and obscure; Things’ essences all there endure. Those essences the truth enfold Of what, when seen, shall then be told. Now it is so; ’twas so of old. Its name⁠—what passes not away; So, in their beautiful array, Things form and never know decay.
How know I that it is so with all the beauties of existing things? By this (nature of the Tao).
